Jules (People Ops): Quick question — I switched my 401(k) deferral from pre-tax to Roth on Nov 12 and payroll cut was Nov 15. Will the Nov 15 payroll contribution come out as Roth or pre-tax? Also, does the employer match follow the employee deferral type?

Riley (Payroll): Typically a deferral change processed before payroll cut is applied, so Nov 15 should be Roth. That said, the downstream vendor feed timing matters — if the record was pulled before our change, it could show old settings. I can check the feed timestamp.

Devon (Benefits): Employer match is plan-level and not a Roth employee contribution — our match posts as a pre-tax employer contribution into the 401(k) account. So match tax treatment is unchanged by your deferral selection. We do not convert employer match to Roth.

Jules (People Ops): Good to know, thanks. One wrinkle: the 401k vendor migration is scheduled for Nov 20. If the vendor ingests payroll on Nov 16 and we swap on Nov 20, could that cause a missed/duplicated contribution for Nov 15?

Riley (Payroll): If migration happens after the payroll file was generated but before reconciliation, there can be edge cases. In prior vendor swaps we sent a manual reconciliation file or issued a corrective retro contribution on the next payroll. I'll pull the previous migration notes (see RFC link in #eng-ops) and confirm timing.

Devon (Benefits): Correct — we have an established corrective flow: 1) vendor reconciliation; 2) if mismatch, manual adjustment / corrective contribution; 3) notify employee with transaction detail. If you want, DM your employee ID and pay period and we'll flag your record so it's monitored during the cutover.

Jules (People Ops): I’ll DM the details. Two quick follow-ups: how are 50+ catch-up contributions handled if I change to Roth? And will HSA payroll deposits be impacted by a 401k deferral change?

Devon (Benefits): Catch-ups are a separate payroll bucket. If you elected Roth for catch-up, it will remain Roth; if you elected pre-tax, it stays pre-tax. Payroll must tag contributions into the right bucket. HSA is independent — changing 401k deferral doesn't alter HSA pre-tax status. If payroll mapping is correct, HSA contributions go to the HSA account as usual.

Jules (People Ops): Awesome, thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick clarifications — I’ll DM my info and check back after Nov 20. :thumbsup:
